title: Geriatric Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Washington School of Medicine
Department: Division of Gerontology & Geriatric Medicine, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Completed ACGME-accredited residency in Family Medicine or Internal Medicine before fellowship start.
International applicants: Non-US citizens welcome to apply; ECFMG status report if applicable.
Application method: ERAS; NRMP Match (code 1918151F0); interviews via Thalamus
Visa support: Per UW GME Visa Policy (linked from programme page)
Summary: Prepares future leaders in geriatric medicine through training at Harborview, VA Puget Sound and UW Medical Center plus PACE, post-acute care and home visits; an integrated two-year geriatrics-palliative option is also offered.

title: Palliative Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Washington School of Medicine
Department: Division of Gerontology & Geriatric Medicine, Department of Medicine
Positions: Up to 5 per year (4 adult track, 1 pediatric track)
Summary: A one-year fellowship training physicians to deliver palliative care for severely and chronically ill patients of all ages across inpatient consult services, palliative care units, long-term care, home hospice and clinics.

title: Hematology-Oncology Fellowship (UW/Fred Hutch)
inst: University of Washington School of Medicine
Department: University of Washington / Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center
Duration: Typically 3 years (dual boards); single-subspecialty and ABIM Research Pathway also considered
Deadline: All materials in ERAS by the date released to programmes (typically third Wednesday in July)
Eligibility: Completed or enrolled in ACGME, ACGME-I, RCPSC, CFPC or AOA internal medicine residency; passed all USMLE/COMLEX exams; commitment to academic medicine; US citizenship or permanent residence by NRMP rank deadline.
International applicants: US citizenship/permanent residence required in most cases (T32 funding); exception possible for classical haematology track.
Application method: ERAS with programme signals (primary screen); NRMP Match
Funding: Partially funded by federal T32 grants; fellows are University of Washington employees
Visa support: Generally unable to sponsor J-1 or H-1B; applicants needing sponsorship with classical haematology interest may be eligible via separate funding.
Summary: An ACGME-accredited fellowship using resources across multiple institutions to prepare fellows for academic careers in basic, translational and clinical research in haematology and oncology.

title: Endocrinology, Metabolism & Nutrition Fellowship
inst: University of Washington School of Medicine
Department: Division of Metabolism, Endocrinology & Nutrition, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Completion of ACGME- or RCPSC-accredited internal medicine residency; eligible for VA Puget Sound appointment (incl. Selective Service where applicable). Research track open only to US citizens/permanent residents.
Application method: ERAS; NRMP Match (Clinical Scholar 1918143F1; Research Scholar 1918143F0)
Funding: Compensation per CIR-NW collective bargaining agreement; see UW GME Prospective Residents & Fellows page (linked from programme page).
Visa support: J-1 and H-1B sponsorship for the two-year clinical scholar track only (per UW GME Visa Policy)
Summary: Trains physicians in diabetes, endocrinology, metabolism and nutrition across UW Medical Center, Harborview and VA Puget Sound, with clinical scholar and research scholar tracks.

title: Nephrology Fellowship
inst: University of Washington School of Medicine
Department: Division of Nephrology, Department of Medicine
Duration: 2 years clinical (research track at least 2 additional years)
Eligibility: US board-certified or board-eligible in Internal Medicine (or ABIM 'exceptionally qualified'); US clinical experience recommended.
Application method: ERAS; NRMP Match; virtual interviews September-October
Positions: 5-6 fellows per year (up to 2 research track)
Funding: Compensation per CIR-NW collective bargaining agreement; see UW GME Prospective Residents & Fellows page (linked from programme page).
Visa support: US citizen, permanent resident or J-1 only; H-1B applicants not considered
Licence requirement: Eligible for Washington State medical licensure
Summary: A highly competitive ACGME-accredited nephrology fellowship with clinical training at Harborview, UW Medical Center and Puget Sound VA plus outpatient dialysis at Northwest Kidney Centers.

title: Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Washington School of Medicine
Department: Division of Pulmonary, Critical Care & Sleep Medicine, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Completed ACGME- or RCPSC-accredited Internal Medicine residency; must be eligible for an NIH T32 stipend.
Application method: ERAS (one track only); signals encouraged; NRMP Match (Physician-scientist 1918156F0, Clinician-educator 1918156F1, Clinical 1918156F2)
Funding: Primarily supported by NIH (T32 stipend eligibility required)
Summary: Trains academic leaders, scientists and scholars in pulmonary and critical care medicine through physician-scientist, clinician-educator and clinical tracks.

title: Sleep Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Washington School of Medicine
Department: Division of Pulmonary, Critical Care & Sleep Medicine, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Board eligible in internal medicine, neurology, psychiatry, otolaryngology, pediatrics, family medicine or anesthesiology.
Summary: A one-year multidisciplinary ACGME-accredited clinical sleep fellowship based at the UW Medicine Sleep Center at Harborview, with training at UWMC, VA Puget Sound and Seattle Children's.

title: Rheumatology Fellowship
inst: University of Washington School of Medicine
Department: Division of Rheumatology, Department of Medicine
Deadline: ERAS; interview invitations early August 2026; interviews 18 August-13 October 2026
Eligibility: Completed (or on track to complete) ACGME-accredited Internal Medicine residency; ABIM certification eligible.
International applicants: IMGs with valid ECFMG certification and active US clinical training welcome.
Application method: ERAS; NRMP Match; virtual interview via Thalamus
Visa support: J-1 sponsored; H-1B only in exceptional circumstances
Licence requirement: Eligible for Washington State medical license before start
Summary: Training rheumatologists since 1967, the UW programme combines nine months of inpatient consults in year one across three Seattle hospitals with individualised clinical, educator and physician-scientist development.

title: Allergy/Immunology Fellowship
inst: Vanderbilt University Medical Center
Department: Division of Allergy, Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine, Department of Medicine
Duration: 2 years (NIH T32 support possible for years 3-5)
Eligibility: Completed residency in internal medicine, pediatrics or medicine/pediatrics.
Funding: Three NIH T32s may support salary for years 3-5 for research-track fellows (competitive)
Summary: A two-year programme training academic clinicians and investigators in allergy and immunology, meeting American Board of Allergy and Immunology certification requirements.

title: Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine Fellowship
inst: Vanderbilt University Medical Center
Department: Division of Allergy, Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine, Department of Medicine
Duration: 3 years (about half complete an optional 4th year)
Funding: T32 support available for a fourth research year
Summary: A three-year programme producing expert clinicians with exceptional research training, customised to research- or clinically-focused academic careers without designated tracks.

title: Endocrinology Clinical Fellowship
inst: Vanderbilt University Medical Center
Department: Division of Diabetes, Endocrinology and Metabolism, Department of Medicine
Application method: ERAS; NRMP Match; three letters of recommendation
Funding: Four weeks paid vacation; 403(b) retirement matched up to 5%; see VUMC GME for house staff benefits
Visa support: J-1 supported; H-1B not supported under most circumstances
Summary: Since 1956, Vanderbilt's individually tailored endocrinology fellowship has trained over 200 graduates for clinical or research careers.

title: Gastroenterology Fellowship
inst: Vanderbilt University Medical Center
Department: Division of Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition, Department of Medicine
Funding: Research track supported by NIH T32 (trainees must be T32-eligible)
Summary: An ACGME-accredited programme training future leaders in academic gastroenterology with clinical and research tracks and an ABIM combined GI/Transplant Hepatology option.

title: Transplant Hepatology Fellowship
inst: Vanderbilt University Medical Center
Department: Division of Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition / Vanderbilt Transplant Center
Visa support: Can consider applicants who need visa sponsorship
Summary: Transplant hepatology training at the Vanderbilt Transplant Center, one of the ten largest US transplant institutes, performing 160-180 liver transplants a year.

title: Hospice and Palliative Care Fellowship
inst: Vanderbilt University Medical Center
Department: Section of Palliative Care, Division of General Internal Medicine and Public Health
Eligibility: Completed ACGME-accredited, AOA-approved, ACGME-I Advanced Specialty-accredited, or RCPSC/CFPC-accredited residency.
Summary: An interdisciplinary, multi-campus programme at VUMC and VA Tennessee Valley that has trained over 30 fellows since 2008, with clinical and research tracks.

title: Geriatric Medicine Fellowship
inst: Vanderbilt University Medical Center
Department: Division of Geriatric Medicine, Department of Medicine
Duration: 1 year clinical (2-year VA advanced/Quality Scholars tracks optional)
Eligibility: Completed ACGME-accredited residency in Internal Medicine or Family Medicine; ACGME-I and non-ACGME IM/FM graduates via the exceptional candidate pathway.
International applicants: ACGME-I and non-ACGME-accredited residency graduates considered via exceptional candidate pathway.
Positions: Up to 4 clinical fellows per year
Summary: An interdisciplinary, multi-campus programme at Vanderbilt Health and VA Tennessee Valley that has trained 49 fellows since 2000, developing leaders in age-friendly healthcare.

title: Hematology and Oncology Fellowship
inst: Vanderbilt University Medical Center
Department: Division of Hematology and Oncology / Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center
Duration: 3 years (combined path); up to 18 months research
Eligibility: Board eligible or certified in Internal Medicine.
Application method: ERAS (no paper applications); few interviews offered to non-signalling applicants
Summary: Provides training in all aspects of clinical haematology and oncology leading to ABIM dual certification, with research opportunities from molecular biology to clinical investigation.

title: Infectious Diseases Fellowship
inst: Vanderbilt University Medical Center
Department: Division of Infectious Diseases, Department of Medicine
Application method: ERAS; NRMP Match; not participating in ERAS programme signalling this cycle
Summary: A fellowship with a clinical consult year at VUMC and the Nashville VA followed by mentored research, within a division with NIH-funded HIV, H. pylori, drug hypersensitivity and mycobacteria programmes.

title: Nephrology Fellowship
inst: Vanderbilt University Medical Center
Department: Division of Nephrology and Hypertension, Department of Medicine
Duration: 2-3 years (two-year clinical track; three-year educator/research tracks)
Funding: NIH T32 training grant for selected fellows
Summary: Provides MD and/or PhD fellows with clinical and research training across AKI, CKD, ESKD, transplantation and paediatrics, tailored to each fellow's career path.

title: Rheumatology Fellowship
inst: Vanderbilt University Medical Center
Department: Division of Rheumatology and Immunology, Department of Medicine
Visa support: Interviews may be granted to applicants requiring J-1 visas
Summary: A two-year ACGME-accredited fellowship providing comprehensive clinical rheumatology training plus instruction in investigative rheumatology and basic science research.

title: Endocrinology, Diabetes & Metabolism Fellowship
inst: Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
Department: Division of Endocrinology, Metabolism & Lipid Research, John T. Milken Department of Medicine
Duration: Not less than 2 years; 3 years strongly recommended
Eligibility: Successful completion of a three-year internal medicine programme; US citizenship or valid visa.
International applicants: Foreign medical graduates must provide proof of passing ECFMG certifying examinations.
Accreditation: Fulfils ACGME and ABIM requirements (clinical track)
Visa support: J-1 and H-1 transfer visas considered depending on funding availability each year
Summary: One of the oldest training programmes in endocrinology, diabetes and metabolism, training academically oriented physicians and scientists through research and clinical training.

title: Allergy & Immunology Fellowship
inst: Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
Department: Division of Allergy and Immunology, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Three years of internal medicine or pediatrics residency, or four years of med/peds; PSTP short-track trainees may apply after two years.
Application method: ERAS; NRMP Match (separate IM and pediatric selection)
Positions: 2 internal medicine and 1 pediatric position per year
Funding: Stipends and benefits maintained by the WashU/Barnes-Jewish/St. Louis Children's GME Consortium (per programme page).
Summary: A two-year ACGME-accredited combined adult and paediatric allergy and immunology fellowship developing future leaders, with faculty from internal medicine and paediatrics.

title: General Gastroenterology Fellowship
inst: Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
Department: Division of Gastroenterology, Department of Medicine
Visa support: Unable to accept H-1B; J-1 accepted for the track not funded by the NIH training grant when appropriate
Summary: A three-year general gastroenterology fellowship within a division reporting 90% of alumni in academic positions, with advanced endoscopy, IBD and hepatology training available afterwards.

title: Geriatric Medicine Fellowship
inst: Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
Department: Division of General Internal Medicine, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Completed three-year ACGME-accredited Internal Medicine or Family Medicine residency, or RCPSC IM / CFPC FM residency, before appointment.
Summary: A small geriatric medicine fellowship developing clinicians and leaders in clinical geriatrics, medical education, aging research and health care improvement, with interdisciplinary team care of older adults.

title: Hematology-Oncology Fellowship
inst: Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
Department: Divisions of Hematology and Oncology, Department of Medicine / Siteman Cancer Center
Positions: 8 new fellows per year, plus 1 Hematology Focused Fellowship Training Program position
Summary: A three-year ACGME-accredited programme training future leaders in academic haematology and oncology using WashU Medicine, Barnes-Jewish Hospital and Siteman Cancer Center, with clinical provider, clinical investigator and laboratory tracks.

title: Infectious Diseases Fellowship
inst: Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
Department: Division of Infectious Diseases, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: MD, MD/PhD, DO or equivalent (e.g., MBBS) and completed accredited internal medicine residency.
International applicants: IMGs with US residency welcome; IMGs with non-US IM residency eligible with valid ECFMG certification and USMLE Step 3 passed at time of application.
Application method: ERAS (July cycle); three letters and personal statement
Summary: A fellow-centred ACGME-accredited programme combining comprehensive clinical ID training with protected scholarly time to develop the next generation of ID leaders.

title: Hospice and Palliative Medicine Fellowship
inst: Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
Department: Division of Palliative Medicine, Department of Medicine
Positions: Adult and pediatric tracks (one fellow per year per track as stated)
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited fellowship with interdisciplinary adult and paediatric teams at Barnes-Jewish Hospital, St. Louis Children's Hospital and Evelyn's House.

title: Pulmonary & Critical Care Medicine Fellowship
inst: Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
Department: Division of Pulmonary & Critical Care Medicine, Department of Medicine
Funding: Training grant fellows receive at least 24 months protected research time
Summary: A three-year fellowship combining broad pulmonary training with multidisciplinary critical care, with 18 months of core clinical rotations and optional physician-scientist research.

title: Adult Rheumatology Fellowship
inst: Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
Department: Division of Rheumatology, Department of Medicine
Summary: Trains rheumatologists to deliver excellent care and advance the field through clinical care, scientific inquiry, education, leadership and advocacy, with career development tracks at Barnes-Jewish Hospital.

title: Nephrology Fellowship
inst: Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
Department: Division of Nephrology, Department of Medicine
Duration: 2 years (research track third year supported by the division)
Funding: $1,200 yearly continuing education stipend; research track third year funded by the division
Summary: A two-year nephrology fellowship with a four-week orientation, inpatient, transplant, specialty and home-modality training, night float and a division-funded research track.

title: Medical Oncology-Hematology Fellowship
inst: Yale School of Medicine
Department: Department of Internal Medicine / Yale Cancer Center
Deadline: ERAS opens in July; application deadline at the end of August
Positions: Includes 1 fellow per year in the ASH Hematology-Focused Fellowship Training Program
Summary: A 36-month programme providing comprehensive clinical training in neoplasia and classical haematology with robust research experience to prepare fellows for academic careers.

title: Hospice & Palliative Medicine Fellowship
inst: Yale School of Medicine
Department: Department of Internal Medicine
Eligibility: Completed ACGME-accredited residency of at least 3 years in surgery, psychiatry, emergency medicine, internal medicine, IM/pediatrics, neurology, radiation oncology, anesthesia, OB/GYN or PM&R with board eligibility/certification.
International applicants: Valid ECFMG certificate required for IMGs.
Application method: ERAS; NRMP Match; signals considered; virtual interviews
Summary: A fellow-centred hospice and palliative medicine fellowship at Yale that matches programme strengths to each fellow's interests, with T32 research opportunities.

title: Infectious Diseases Fellowship
inst: Yale School of Medicine
Department: Section of Infectious Diseases, Department of Internal Medicine
Duration: Multiple tracks; ABIM Research Pathway track includes four fellowship years
Summary: An ACGME-accredited programme offering clinical ID training with emphasis on education and investigation across Yale New Haven Hospital and VA Connecticut, preparing academic clinicians, educators and physician scientists.

title: Rheumatology Fellowship
inst: Yale School of Medicine
Department: Section of Rheumatology, Allergy & Immunology, Department of Internal Medicine
Duration: Typically 2 years clinical; traditional fellowship includes 2+ years of research
Summary: Yale's rheumatology fellowship develops academic and clinical leaders, preparing fellows as physician scientists or expert clinicians and educators in rheumatology, allergy and immunology.

title: Gastroenterology and Hepatology Fellowship
inst: Yale School of Medicine
Department: Section of Digestive Diseases, Department of Internal Medicine
Summary: A three-year ACGME-accredited fellowship with a clinical first year at Yale New Haven Hospital and VA Connecticut, followed by clinical or research track training.

title: Advanced Transplant Hepatology Fellowship
inst: Yale School of Medicine
Department: Section of Digestive Diseases, Department of Internal Medicine
Eligibility: Completed general gastroenterology fellowship at ACGME-accredited or equivalent programme; eligible for ABIM Gastroenterology Board.
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited fellowship at the Yale New Haven Transplantation Center with intensive training in adult, paediatric and living donor liver transplantation.

title: Clinical Endocrinology Fellowship
inst: Yale School of Medicine
Department: Section of Endocrinology & Metabolism, Department of Internal Medicine
Application method: ERAS only; CV, personal statement, three letters
Summary: A two-year clinical endocrinology fellowship with about 22 months of inpatient consult and outpatient clinic training plus a scholarly project, alongside a three-year traditional track.

title: Geriatric Medicine Clinical Fellowship
inst: Yale School of Medicine
Department: Section of Geriatrics, Department of Internal Medicine
Deadline: ERAS opens for subspecialties in July
Summary: Geriatric medicine fellows rotate across inpatient, outpatient and community settings affiliated with Yale New Haven Hospital and VA Connecticut, with an emphasis on interdisciplinary, Age-Friendly care.

title: Clinical Nephrology Fellowship
inst: Yale School of Medicine
Department: Section of Nephrology, Department of Internal Medicine
Eligibility: Completed three-year ACGME-accredited internal medicine residency by fellowship start.
Application method: ERAS only; interview slots allocated by timing of receipt
Summary: A two-year nephrology academic clinician track focused on clinical skills, teaching and education, with inpatient rotations in year one and flexible inpatient/outpatient training in year two.

title: Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine Fellowship
inst: Yale School of Medicine
Department: Section of Pulmonary, Critical Care and Sleep Medicine, Department of Internal Medicine
Duration: 3 years (36 months; option to extend for research)
Eligibility: Completed accredited three-year internal medicine residency.
Funding: Division T32 NIH training grant supports advanced research training
Summary: A three-year PCCM fellowship with at least 18 months of clinical training and 18 months of scholarly activity, supported by an NIH T32 grant.

title: ACGME Adult Infectious Diseases Fellowship
inst: Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine
Department: Division of Infectious Diseases, Department of Medicine
Duration: Typically 3 years (year 1 clinical; later years research)
Summary: Founded in 1981, a fellowship that typically spans three years with a clinical first year followed by research, preparing fellows for careers in academic medicine and public health.

title: Gastroenterology Fellowship
inst: Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine
Department: Division of Gastroenterology and Hepatology, Department of Medicine
Summary: A three-year fellowship with clinical and research tracks at The Johns Hopkins Hospital and Johns Hopkins Bayview, training leaders in academic and clinical gastroenterology.

title: Infectious Diseases Fellowship
inst: University of Michigan Medical School (Michigan Medicine)
Department: Division of Infectious Diseases, Department of Internal Medicine
Deadline: ERAS opens early July; programme receives applications mid-July; virtual interviews August-October
Application method: ERAS; three letters (one from programme director or chair)
Visa support: Minimum J-1 visa status required; H-1B applicants not considered
Summary: An ACGME-accredited programme blending clinical and research training at University Hospital and the VA Ann Arbor, with tracks in medical education, transplant ID, antimicrobial stewardship and research.

title: Infectious Diseases Fellowship
inst: University of California, San Francisco (UCSF)
Department: Division of Infectious Diseases, Department of Medicine
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (UCSF Department of Medicine lists 21 ACGME-accredited fellowships)
Funding: Research supported by multiple NIH T32 training grants
Summary: UCSF's ID fellowship trains leaders in research, public health, global health, stewardship, clinical ID and education across UCSF Medical Center, Zuckerberg San Francisco General and the SF VA.

title: Advanced Benign Gynecologic Surgery Fellowship
inst: University of Toronto – St. Joseph's Health Centre (Unity Health Toronto)
Department: Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Temerty Faculty of Medicine, University of Toronto
Eligibility: Must have fulfilled FRCSC requirements and hold an independent medical licence from the province of Ontario
International applicants: Not stated on official page (FRCSC and independent Ontario licence required)
Application method: Apply via the CanSAGE fellowship match (cansage.org); selection includes interview and site visit in early summer
Licence requirement: Independent medical licence from the province of Ontario
Summary: A 2-year MIGS fellowship at St. Joseph's Health Centre focused on complex benign gynaecologic surgery including large fibroid uteri and stage IV endometriosis.

title: Advanced Gynaecologic Surgery Fellowship
inst: University of Toronto – Mount Sinai Hospital, Women's College Hospital & Trillium Health Partners
Department: Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Temerty Faculty of Medicine, University of Toronto
Deadline: Application form submitted between June 17 and August 15 each year (CanSAGE match)
Eligibility: Canadian-trained graduates only at the current time
International applicants: Not accepted – currently only accepting applications from Canadian-trained graduates
Licence requirement: Certificate of registration with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO); internationally trained physicians must complete the 4–12-week Pre-Entry Assessment Program (PEAP) before full acceptance (department application guidelines)
Summary: A two-year fellowship in advanced gynaecologic surgery training pelvic surgeons across benign gynaecology and complex surgical obstetrics.

title: Advanced Gynaecologic Surgery and Health Quality Improvement Fellowship
inst: University of Toronto – North York General Hospital
Department: Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Temerty Faculty of Medicine, University of Toronto
Deadline: Application form on CanSAGE website submitted between June 17 and August 15 each year
Eligibility: Completed FRCS(C) requirements and an independent practice licence from the Province of Ontario
International applicants: Not stated on official page (FRCS(C) and independent Ontario licence required)
Accreditation: Part of the CanSAGE matching process
Licence requirement: Independent practice licence from the Province of Ontario
Summary: A one-year fellowship at North York General Hospital in advanced gynaecologic surgery combined with health quality improvement.

title: Advanced High-Risk Obstetrics Fellowship
inst: University of Toronto – St. Michael's Hospital (Unity Health Toronto)
Department: Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Temerty Faculty of Medicine, University of Toronto
Deadline: Fellowship Application Form (PDF) by May 1 each year
Application method: Fellowship Application Form (PDF) submitted to the program director; appointment processed through U of T PGME (OATS). Allow 5–6 months processing for international applicants.
Licence requirement: Certificate of registration with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO); internationally trained physicians must complete the 4–12-week Pre-Entry Assessment Program (PEAP) before full acceptance (department application guidelines)
Summary: A one-year fellowship in high-risk obstetrics with a special focus on obstetric ultrasound, training specialists to consult on complicated pregnancies.

title: Advanced Hospitalist Obstetrics Fellowship
inst: University of Toronto – Mount Sinai Hospital (Sinai Health)
Department: Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Temerty Faculty of Medicine, University of Toronto
Deadline: Fellowship Application Form (PDF) by August 31 each year
Eligibility: Overseas-trained graduate specialists in Obstetrics and Gynaecology; fellows function at the level of a Canadian PGY2–3 resident
International applicants: Yes – the fellowship is intended for overseas-trained graduate specialists in Obstetrics and Gynaecology
Application method: Fellowship Application Form (PDF) submitted to the program director; appointment processed through U of T PGME (OATS). Allow 5–6 months processing for international applicants.
Licence requirement: Certificate of registration with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO); internationally trained physicians must complete the 4–12-week Pre-Entry Assessment Program (PEAP) before full acceptance (department application guidelines)
Summary: A 1–2 year fellowship giving overseas-trained obstetrician-gynaecologists experience of North American tertiary obstetric hospitalist practice at Mount Sinai Hospital.

title: CanSAGE Advanced Gynaecologic Surgery Fellowship
inst: University of Toronto – St. Michael's Hospital (Unity Health Toronto)
Department: Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Temerty Faculty of Medicine, University of Toronto
Eligibility: FRCSC; full licence to practise in Ontario; medical degree; CMPA coverage
International applicants: Not accepted – St. Michael's Hospital is not taking out-of-country or IMG applicants for the foreseeable future
Accreditation: CanSAGE (Canadian Society for the Advancement of Gynecologic Excellence)
Application method: Centralized through the CanSAGE Fellowship Match
Licence requirement: Full licence to practise in Ontario; CMPA coverage
Summary: A two-year advanced gynaecologic surgery fellowship at St. Michael's Hospital covering laparoscopic, vaginal, hysteroscopic, open and robotic-assisted approaches.

title: Complex Family Planning Fellowship (CAARE)
inst: University of Toronto – Women's College Hospital, Sinai Health & North York General Hospital
Department: Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Temerty Faculty of Medicine, University of Toronto
Duration: 2 years, with concurrent completion of a master's degree or equivalent
Deadline: January 14, 2026 (application form to obgyn@utoronto.ca, subject "CAARE Fellowship"); program offered every two years
Eligibility: Fulfilled FRCS(C) requirements and an independent medical licence from the province of Ontario; preference for those planning an academic career
International applicants: Exceptional candidates from outside Canada considered if they show potential and are self-funded
Accreditation: Objectives aligned with Society of Family Planning (SFP) Complex Family Planning fellowships
Application method: Fellowship Application Form (PDF) submitted to the program director; appointment processed through U of T PGME (OATS). Allow 5–6 months processing for international applicants.
Funding: Not stated on official page (applicants from outside Canada must be self-funded)
Licence requirement: Certificate of registration with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO); internationally trained physicians must complete the 4–12-week Pre-Entry Assessment Program (PEAP) before full acceptance (department application guidelines)
Summary: A 2-year academic Complex Family Planning (Contraception, Abortion, Advocacy, Research and Education) fellowship with concurrent master's degree, offered every two years.

title: Complex Obstetric Surgery Fellowship
inst: University of Toronto – Mount Sinai Hospital & Credit Valley Hospital
Department: Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Temerty Faculty of Medicine, University of Toronto
Deadline: Application form and all documents by August 1 each year
Eligibility: Canadian medical graduates with an independent CPSO licence and specialist qualifications in Obstetrics and Gynaecology encouraged to apply
International applicants: IMGs with funding support may be considered if a local applicant is not identified; must demonstrate outstanding surgical skills (case logs, references)
Application method: Fellowship Application Form (PDF) submitted to the program director; appointment processed through U of T PGME (OATS). Allow 5–6 months processing for international applicants.
Funding: Not stated on official page (IMGs require funding support)
Licence requirement: Certificate of registration with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO); internationally trained physicians must complete the 4–12-week Pre-Entry Assessment Program (PEAP) before full acceptance (department application guidelines)
Summary: A 1–2 year fellowship based at Mount Sinai Hospital training consultants in the diagnosis and surgical management of complex obstetric surgery in pregnancy.

title: Fetal Neuroimaging Fellowship
inst: University of Toronto – Mount Sinai Hospital & The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids)
Department: Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Temerty Faculty of Medicine, University of Toronto
Eligibility: Certification in Maternal–Fetal Medicine (or equivalent subspecialty radiology training); extensive fetal anomaly scanning experience; research track record
Application method: Fellowship Application Form (PDF) submitted to the program director; appointment processed through U of T PGME (OATS). Allow 5–6 months processing for international applicants.
Licence requirement: Certificate of registration with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO); internationally trained physicians must complete the 4–12-week Pre-Entry Assessment Program (PEAP) before full acceptance (department application guidelines)
Summary: A one-year joint Mount Sinai–SickKids program in fetal brain ultrasound, MRI and multidisciplinary neurodevelopmental care.

title: Global Women's Health and Equity Fellowship
inst: University of Toronto – Women's College Hospital (Toronto) & Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital (Eldoret, Kenya)
Department: Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Temerty Faculty of Medicine, University of Toronto
Start: September 1, 2026 (or alternative date agreed with the Fellowship Director)
Eligibility: Graduates of Canadian or American Obstetrics and Gynaecology residency programs
International applicants: Not accepted – applicants must be graduates of Canadian or American ObGyn residency programs
Application method: Fellowship Application Form (PDF) submitted to the program director; appointment processed through U of T PGME (OATS). Allow 5–6 months processing for international applicants.
Licence requirement: Certificate of registration with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO); internationally trained physicians must complete the 4–12-week Pre-Entry Assessment Program (PEAP) before full acceptance (department application guidelines)
Summary: A 2-year certificate subspecialty program training obstetrician-gynaecologists to improve care for marginalized women locally and internationally, including 9–12 months with AMPATH in Eldoret, Kenya.

title: Gynaecologic Oncology Fellowship (RCPSC)
inst: University of Toronto – Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre & Princess Margaret Cancer Centre (UHN)
Department: Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Temerty Faculty of Medicine, University of Toronto
Duration: 3 years (2 clinical years plus a mandatory academic third year)
Accreditation: Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada (RCPSC) subspecialty program
Application method: Fellowship Application Form (PDF) submitted to the program director; appointment processed through U of T PGME (OATS). Allow 5–6 months processing for international applicants.
Licence requirement: Certificate of registration with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO); internationally trained physicians must complete the 4–12-week Pre-Entry Assessment Program (PEAP) before full acceptance (department application guidelines)
Summary: A 2-year clinical gynaecologic oncology fellowship with a mandatory third academic year, leading to the Royal College subspecialty examination.

title: Gynaecologic Reproductive Endocrinology & Infertility Fellowship (RCPSC)
inst: University of Toronto – Mount Sinai Hospital (Sinai Health)
Department: Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Temerty Faculty of Medicine, University of Toronto
Duration: 2 years (optional 3rd year for a Master's via the CIP program)
Deadline: Page lists March 31, 2025 for the July 2026 program (check for the current cycle)

Duration: Indicative 24 months; up to 36 months for a full-time trainee entering at ST5 with minimal relevant experience (competency-based)
Deadline: Per individual post advert (usually advertised in the BMJ)
Eligibility: UK NTN (or equivalent) with clinical training to ST4/ST5 and ARCP outcome 1; or UK CCT/Portfolio Pathway and on (or entitled to) the UK Specialist Register in O&G; or EEA/non-UK applicants listed on the UK Specialist Register in O&G
International applicants: Only non-UK applicants already on the UK Specialist Register in O&G are eligible; those requiring a work permit only if no other suitable candidates
Accreditation: RCOG Subspecialty Curriculum 2024 (leads to RCOG subspecialty accreditation; part of CCT in O&G)
Application method: Apply directly to the Deaneries/Trusts as set out in adverts (usually in the BMJ); open competition with structured interview; register with the RCOG Subspecialty Committee on appointment
Visa support: Non-UK/non-EEA nationals requiring a work permit are subject to the resident labour market test and considered only if no other suitable candidates; individual Deaneries decide immigration evidence required
Licence requirement: GMC registration with a licence to practise (UK NTN or UK Specialist Register in O&G)
Summary: RCOG subspecialty training (SST) in Gynaecological Oncology, one of four O&G subspecialty programmes completed in the final years of UK training to develop consultant-level skills.

title: Post-CSCST Fellowship in Paediatric Critical Care Medicine
inst: Children's Health Ireland (CHI at Crumlin and Temple Street)

title: Postgraduate Training in Paediatric Intensive Care Medicine
inst: Hôpitaux Universitaires de Genève (HUG) - Hôpital des enfants

Summary: SIWF-registered postgraduate training in paediatric intensive care at HUG's multidisciplinary PICU, a centre for highly specialised medicine caring for patients from extreme prematurity to 16 years, including congenital heart disease and paediatric liver transplantation.

title: Postgraduate Training in Paediatric Intensive Care Medicine

Summary: Category A postgraduate paediatric intensive care training at CHUV's multidisciplinary university PICU for children aged 0-18, with individualised training plans and rotations in partner units in Switzerland and abroad.

Summary: One-year fellowship at staff level in UZ Gent's 42-bed NICU caring for about 650 newborns a year, including neonatal transport and pre/post-operative care for congenital heart surgery.

title: Postgraduate Training in Paediatric Cardiology and Paediatric Intensive Care (Weiterbildung Kinderkardiologie / Pädiatrische Intensivmedizin)

Summary: Authorised postgraduate training in paediatric cardiology and paediatric intensive care at the Centre for Congenital Heart Disease of HDZ NRW, with EMAH training and research in collaboration with Ruhr-Universität Bochum.

title: Cardiothoracic Imaging Fellowship
inst: UCLA Health

Licence requirement: Must qualify for a California medical licence prior to the start of fellowship.
Summary: A new cardiothoracic imaging fellowship preparing radiologists to be independent cardiothoracic specialists, with a regular path (6 months thoracic, 6 months cardiac) or an IR path including thoracic interventions.

title: Diagnostic Neuroradiology Fellowship
inst: UCLA Health
Department: Department of Radiological Sciences, David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA (Diagnostic Neuroradiology)

title: Interventional Neuroradiology Fellowship

International applicants: Not ACGME accredited, so only US citizens or Green Card holders can be trained.
Application method: UCLA Recruit online application; interviews up to 3 years before start.
Visa support: No visa sponsorship (US citizens or Green Card holders only).
Licence requirement: Must qualify for a California medical licence prior to the start of fellowship.
Summary: A 2-year CAST-certified neuroendovascular surgery fellowship accepting candidates from radiology, neurology and neurosurgery backgrounds.

title: Body Imaging Fellowship
inst: UCSF Health

Eligibility: Completion of a four-year diagnostic radiology residency from an accredited program.
International applicants: Graduates of medical schools outside the US or Canada must hold a valid ECFMG certificate at the time of application, be eligible for a California Medical License and have passed USMLE Steps I, II and III (or COMLEX/LMCC equivalent).

Visa support: The University sponsors J-1 ECFMG visas for fellowship positions in the majority of cases.
Licence requirement: Radiology board certification (or board eligibility) and a California Medical License are required prior to appointment.
Summary: The UCSF Body Imaging fellowship provides comprehensive and structured training in all aspects of abdominal and pelvic imaging, maximising learning in advanced multimodality imaging using MRI, CT, PET and ultrasound.
